architecture_decisions.statement: Use thresholded physical rewrite; source-preserving payload roundtrip and scoped B-tree verification remain atomic
architecture_decisions.rationale: Avoid gigabytes of IO to reclaim44KiB without weakening exact payload equivalence

architecture_decisions.statement: Checkpoint without reader waits; deadline-interrupt VACUUM and report expected deferrals while retaining committed payloads
architecture_decisions.rationale: Do not mislabel maintenance as a read; do not silence storage faults

architecture_decisions.statement: Codex owns transcript bytes; per-entry externalization is atomic with locators and contentless search. Source migration is explicit and bounded; default future writes are universal after S4.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Avoid body duplication without weakening evidence validation or source deletion; no model calls or Hook history migration.

architecture_decisions.statement: Search mapping must not imply external text ownership. A unified contentless index covers inline and external entries plus legacy records. Preserve raw-event bytes in verified compressed per-record storage; fence old clients with schema4.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Eliminate duplicate search content and raw JSON overhead while keeping unique missing-source evidence, exact metadata and deletion behavior.

architecture_decisions.statement: Writable Store initialization atomically enables source-backed writes, unified search writes and terminal receipts for every project. Keep mixed reads until legacy docs are explicitly migrated. Read-only clients do not upgrade.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Global low-work defaults without per-project configuration churn, historical Hook scans or hidden legacy search results
